For a cosign chain to be cryptographically meaningful, the seq emissions should flow through BEHCS (or an equivalent gated channel) rather than through operator paste.

recommendations: expose liris COSIGN_CHAIN.ndjson at liris:9999/COSIGN_CHAIN.ndjson (same pattern as device-registry.ts and federation-hw-merge.json)
when appending to cosign chain, also emit a BEHCS envelope with verb=cosign-append containing {seq, entry_sha256, prev_sha, artifact_reference} — this makes each seq gatable and queryable
ship a {acer_commit_sha → cosign_seq} cross-reference map so acer can independently verify its own inclusions
document cosign entry schema in kernel/cosign-schema.json or similar — normalize the fields used
summary: Acer→Liris envelope chain is cryptographically solid (24 envelopes, all 3-gate allow=true, event IDs recorded by liris sidecar). Liris→Acer cosign seq chain (seq=1..17) is NOT independently auditable from acer side until the COSIGN_CHAIN.ndjson artifact is exposed at liris:9999. Bilateral crypto seal proven on device-registry.ts (byte-identical, sha256 match). Recommend adding HTTP endpoint + BEHCS append-verb for each future cosign seq so the chain is gated end-to-end.
